title: Kestrel and the Postcard
premise: Hazel Ravensworth, a marine biologist who fled a scandal that cost him his reputation and nearly his freedom, has spent three years on a small island counting turtles and keeping his life deliberately small. When his sister blackmails him into bringing a date to the family reunion, he hires Kestrel, a sharp-tongued ferry mechanic with secrets of her own, to play along. The fake romance turns real by dessert, but Hazel's past resurfaces when the man who destroyed him arrives on the island seeking a favor only Hazel can grant. Choosing between quiet survival and public justice, Hazel testifies, loses the career he was quietly rebuilding, and gains something better: Kestrel misses the last ferry of the season on purpose, choosing to stay.
about_author: Jonah Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former coastal researcher who traded tide charts for typewriters after a decade of fieldwork in the North Atlantic. They write romances about people who mistake safety for happiness.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Three years after a whistleblower scandal gutted his career, Hazel lives by routine: nest surveys, early tides, no attachments. A letter from his mother announces the family reunion and a pointed reminder that he'll be arriving alone. The emotional beat is brittle calm — a life built to be unbreakable because it's unbearably small.

chapters.title: The Ferry Mechanic
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel Okafor fixes engines on the island ferry and keeps her own history locked tight. When Hazel awkwardly offers cash for one evening of pretending, she laughs in his face — then names an outrageous price, mostly to see if he'll flinch. He doesn't. The beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's armor.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over bad coffee they negotiate rules: no real names of exes, no touching unless required, leave before sentiment sets in. Each rule reveals more than it hides. Hazel admits the reunion is really an ambush by relatives who testified against him; Kestrel goes quiet at the word 'testified.' Beat: intimacy disguised as paperwork.

chapters.title: The Ravensworth Reunion
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Kestrel plays the girlfriend flawlessly — disarming his aunt, charming his hostile brother-in-law, who happens to be the lawyer who once represented the company Hazel exposed. By dessert, the performance has stopped feeling like one: their hands find each other without instruction. Beat: warmth arriving like a trap springing shut.

chapters.title: Missed Trains
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She stays the night — ostensibly missing the last train, actually choosing to. Dawn on the breakwater, confessions in fragments: she once took money to stay silent about something, and it's the thing she can't forgive herself for. Hazel doesn't judge; he recognizes. Beat: the fake date becoming a real beginning.

chapters.title: The Man from the Company
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Marcus Hale, the executive Hazel's testimony nearly imprisoned, walks into the island's only pub. He's out on appeal, hunting for the missing ledger page that could overturn his conviction — and he knows Hazel kept copies. He makes an offer wrapped around a threat. Beat: the safe life revealed as never having existed.

chapters.title: What Kestrel Knows
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Her old silence connects to Hale's company — the hush money she took years ago bought the cover-up Hazel tried to expose. Telling him means losing him; not telling means becoming what she despises. She puts the truth on his kitchen table and waits. Beat: terror and relief braided together.

chapters.title: The Ledger Page
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hale escalates: sabotage at the ferry yard, an anonymous call to Hazel's old regulator threatening new charges. Hazel realizes the missing ledger page isn't leverage — it's evidence that completes the case against Hale. Using it means exposure, headlines, the end of invisibility. Beat: rising dread and hardening resolve.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax. At the appellate hearing, Hazel surrenders the ledger page and testifies again, this time with Kestrel beside him and Kestrel's own statement read into the record. Hale's appeal collapses; Hazel's career prospects collapse with it. Walking out, hollowed and lighter, he finds he doesn't regret it. Beat: justice outside the law's timetable, paid for in full.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. Winter closes the island route. On the dock, Kestrel holds a ticket for the final crossing — then lets the ferry leave without her. 'I'm done surviving,' she says. Hazel, unemployed and unhidden, takes her hand in front of everyone. Beat: the price of survival finally refunded as love.
